newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-KARNATAKA BOWLERS DOMINATE OPENING DAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KARNATAKA BOWLERS DOMINATE OPENING DAY.

text.p: Karnataka off-spinner
Rangarao Ananth took four wickets for 72 to bundle out South
Africa for 243 on the opening day of their three-day match on
Sunday.
But the South African bowlers struck back in the last
session of play to reduce Ranji Trophy champions Karantaka to 87
for four at the close.
South African batsmen, electing to bat first after skipper
Hansie Cronje won the toss, failed to master the Karnataka
attack and none of them managed to reach the half-century mark
in the face of some tight bowling by Ananth.
Cronje and Jonty Rhodes were top scorers with 46 apiece and
were dismissed by Ananth when they had looked set to make big
scores.
Cronje struck four boundaries in his 69-ball knock, while
Rhodes hit seven fours in 56 balls.
Medium-pacer David Johnson claimed three wickets for 76 runs
and left-arm spinner Anand Katti bagged two for 43.
Derek Crookes hit a brisk 45 off 39 balls before becoming
the first of Katti's victims.
Karnataka batsmen fumbled against pace bowlers Allan Donald
and Lance Klusener. Only Fazal Khaleel showed some resistance
with 32 before test batsman Rahul Dravid and Parambathe
Shashikanth steadied the innings.
